version.changelog: Sanitized public runbook update with service-user diagnostics, ClawHub Codex extension drift checks, isolated Codex-home guidance, and generic shared-repo wording.

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent OpenClaw update runbook, but parts of its troubleshooting guidance can expose live channel tokens in terminal or agent transcripts.

dimensions.detail: Reading OpenClaw state, logs, plugin records, service env files, and config is expected for this runbook, but printing raw token fields and advising exact line-byte sharing is broader exposure than needed for diagnosing quote corruption.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is markdown/YAML documentation with no executable installer, lifecycle script, dependency manifest, remote payload fetch, or hidden install behavior observed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Most instructions are scoped to OpenClaw update recovery and emphasize verification, but agents/openai.yaml allows implicit invocation and the artifact does not consistently require explicit user confirmation before high-impact maintenance or secret-inspection steps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discusses service managers, cron state, plugin updates, sudo-as-service-user diagnostics, and killing orphan update shells as operational recovery topics; I did not find instructions to install unauthorized persistence or backdoors, but the maintenance authority is high impact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The update, repair, plugin, service, SSH, and log-inspection workflows match the stated OpenClaw maintenance purpose, but the reference runbook includes credential-handling steps that print token-bearing config/env lines and recommends temporary plaintext token fallbacks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use it only for explicit OpenClaw maintenance tasks, require confirmation before updates/restarts/config edits, and do not run token-inspection commands that print raw values. If a token has already appeared in a transcript, support ticket, log, or backup, rotate it and remove plaintext fallbacks after recovery.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced failure-patterns file is present in the artifact bundle and was inspected; the local reference is part of the documented install model, not evasion.
[RA1] expected: The self-update references describe hazards when OpenClaw updates the gateway it is running under; they are warnings and recovery guidance, not skill self-modification.
[PE3] unexpected: Credential inspection is relevant to channel recovery, but the artifact-backed commands can print live token values and one workaround advises inlining a literal token into config, which creates unnecessary plaintext exposure.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Implicit invocation is not hidden, but it is under-scoped for a runbook that may lead to updates, restarts, config edits, and token inspection.
[RA2] expected: The persistence-related text is mainly about detecting existing cron, LaunchAgent, service, and orphan shell behavior during updates; I did not find instructions to create unauthorized persistent access.
[PE2] expected: The sudo example is limited to running diagnostics as the gateway service user so commands inspect the same state as the managed service; it is elevated but purpose-aligned.
[T09] unexpected: The static finding is supported: the failure-patterns reference includes commands and sharing guidance that can disclose authentication tokens through stdout, transcripts, logs, or support artifacts.
